I believe we need to begin looking underneath all of the rugs and behind all of the curtains to launch the doubtless shocking and sobering review into the real intentions and the real agendas that provide the fuel to what is in fact an oppressive ruling coalition, and to ask it of the question, who and what do you really serve? And we need to ask ourselves and to ask each other, what is really going on here? And why from system to system and institution to institution is there absolute systemic erosion, malfunction, debilitation, injustice, discrimination, corruption, racism, and inequality? And how and why has sterile indifference, disharmony, and strife become our routine and daily experience? What has proven recurrently to pander only to experience, the false hope of change, to offer promises that have never been kept, to escape accountability, to pillage, to plunder, to hoard, to kick the can, to be wasteful, to capitalize on, alienate, and betray its own citizens needs, alas, to be called to answer. And not only in this inquisition should we stop listening to the incessant babble and the tiresome and misleading rhetoric spilling forth from all of the primary agencies of socialization, but each should be muted and silenced from the discord of its overbearing and questionably dignified influence. As each, at least for the time being, needs to release us out from underneath their pressures and to ease up on the burdens they cause and the stories they tell, to stand down and to stop commanding us, to stop controlling us, to stop informing us, anointing us, lying to us, preaching to us, confusing us, exhausting us, and impoverishing us. We need to be able to distance ourselves and reorient, and we need to be able to take time to breathe and to take in life and feel what it means to just be, To live without a sword down our throats, without guilt, without tax, without deadline, without fear, without anxiety, and without shame. If we are to find reprieve from the control mechanisms that both overtly and covertly dictate our lives, and if it is freedom that we truly seek, we must first be willing to recognize the severity of the impact the collective of the modern institutional agencies has had on our lives, our perceptions, and our thinking. We must acknowledge that throughout the course of our indoctrination into the perspectives of established educational, religious, social, and political precedents, our cognitions have been influenced towards a prejudicial, overly reverent, self righteous, and pious disposition towards institutional intention and our own belief systems. That fundamental to our indoctrination into standardized subjugation, there is an instinctual presupposition that the doctrines of the institution are distinguished and vulnerable, and that our allegiance by virtue of established high and unparalleled valuation is appropriate, dutiful, respectful, and necessary. And we trustingly and we faithfully consume all that we are provided by the predominant and established order. And we rapidly develop staunch and impenetrable opinions and beliefs that align exclusively with the imposition of established dogmatic orthodoxy, and thereby become alienated in our thinking from anything but the positions of its convincingly and fiercely authoritative discourses. Our convictions are not our own. As we only believe what it is we have been told to believe, and from early in our development, from early in our development, the persuasion of our perceptions began. And as the shaping and molding of our young and impressionable minds are set upon, we unwittingly adopt the indoctrination of all of our limited but socially acceptable and suitable attitudes, behaviors, and beliefs. Our impressions, our judgments, our understandings of most things have not been formulated out of free and contemplative thinking nor reflective and thoughtful meditation, that they instead have been dictated to us by forces outside of ourselves. And our entire world views are but the renderings cultivated by the influence of modern institutional interpretation. Our realities are the disciplined and concluded products of the numerous agencies within which our minds have been indoctrinated and prepared. And it is the persistence of established systemical and directed fundamental civil, religious, and scientific principles that there exist an ongoing and unquestioned persuasion towards devotion. And it is also through the widespread mutual and contagious deference that these ideologies become reinforced, inserting by their popularity a convincing and absolute sense of authenticity. And the adherence that we each have to our set of beliefs and our perceptions and how contestable we believe their incorruptibility further produces a profound presumption of righteous legitimacy and credibility. And there is an overly gratuitous and misplaced loyalty towards not only what we hold to be absolute or probable in the universe, but also towards the trustworthiness, the credibility, and the reliability of established proposal, approach, and conclusion. Within our learned perspectives, there exists the inference that the nature of our governing educational and religious models are, of course, with benevolent and gracious intention. And we are conditioned to believe that naturally the aim of each modern institutional constituent is to actually impart the truth, the justice, the healthcare, the wisdom, the assistance, the opportunity, education that is claimed. And that even with blatant and gross ineffectiveness and underperformance and ongoing inadequate results, we still believe that at least the models are sound and that the theory and the systems, though agreeably broken, proceed from a position of goodwill and integrity. We believe that morally, the system is devoted to us, and whereas it may ceaselessly fail us, that at least it strives and aspires towards something better, and that ultimately its goal is to deliver us its struggling dependence from all of our difficulties, our hardships, and to assist and to facilitate for us an elevated standard of living, to make better our situations, to solve and remove for us our problems, our disputes, and our ignorance, and to provide for us our liberty, our health, and our happiness. However, the nature of the modern establishment can be characterized not at all by its nourishing generosity, its charitable kindness, its equitable objectives, or by any genuine endeavor to enhance the wellness, the affluence, or awareness of its subjects. I believe that it is instead the function of the institution to lead us towards authorized compilations of explicitly prearranged dogmatic ideals and conclusions, and to fiercely shepherd our world views towards the prejudice of established tradition. That without doubt, its ambitions are to encourage and to assemble consistent and controlled perceptions of reality, that out of loyal and trusting indenture to authoritative methodologies, we become bound by its infrastructure of discriminating and governing principles as the basis for which we relate to the universe and ourselves. And I believe that all investment, all faith, all deference in prevailing conventional opinion inevitably results in the formation of skeptical, narrow minded, complacent, and irreverent attitudes towards life, existence, ourselves, and each other. That by the disposition of orthodox, scientific, and traditional religious doctrines, there is confessed an industriously treacherous, premeditated, and sinister strategy to ruthlessly disenfranchise us from all things truthful, fruitful, and beyond the realm of science. And that each of us and that each of its organizations, agendas, programs, models and plans have been brought forth out of these streams of influence and intention and are in fact only presenting as being damaged and broken. And that what is in appearance injury, injustice, inequality, misguidance, misappropriation, underfunding, instability, confusion, destitution, and decay is in reality only the natural characteristic unfolding and maturation process of something that is essentially at its very core rooted in annihilative and erroneous thinking, abusive exploitation, and malignant deception. And that all efforts to rehabilitate, to improve upon, or restore these systems are but ongoing distractions, feeding us a false hope of better and brighter days to come. That all of the things that have been failing us, all of the things that are failing us are going to continue to fail us because they are meant to. This has never been, nor will it ever be, a healthy or just system, never an honest, equal, or fair system, never plentiful, never enriching, never has it upheld its citizens, never has its wealth or its resource been committed to a true easing of our burdens. And in order to facilitate any true effective liberating outcomes, and never has it affected the fundamental change or even demonstrated the competence competency, the capacity, or the compassion to do so. And all of the fights that we think we have won and all of the progress we think we have made are but the stifled concessions of an intelligent warden knowing that we, too, must sometimes eat. The essential nature of our contemporary human environment can be evidenced by its vast inventory of characteristically flawed, imbalanced, and depraved systems of the institution. It is in part the collective propensity of these systems towards instability, dilapidation, corruption, misappropriation, and domineering that we are given a beginning glimpse into the heart and personality of this indecent dictatorial machine. The astringent distillate of our structured and subordinate experience within the establishment, with its native, adverse, and encumbering regulations and controls, its pretentious supremacy, its predatory disposition, shows us that through these and other predominant and characteristic features, its inclination is far apart from being benevolent, moral, or righteous. That across the board, whether it be courtroom, bank, DMV, hospital, or prison, all institutional formations under the directives of institutional intention and control can be inarguably qualified as devoid of regard, devoid of grace, devoid of purity, and devoid of pure of true goodness. And that as spiritless institutions, there is a characteristically dull, dispassionate, callous, and imperious pulse that is rudimentary to the mechanized emotionless experience that is our subjugated subordination. The manner with which the establishment manages us can be characterized by indifference, preeminence, constraint, judgment, always impersonal, always harsh, strict, cold, and rigid. We are fully influenced by the prominence of this disparaging, crude, and congenial demeanor as found within most institutional experiences as they both demonstrate and exemplify the acceptability of disregard and detachment as routine practices in relating to our fellow human beings. And it is not we, the 99%, the indentured servants, the debt slaves, the influenced that are lacking in goodness and in grace, as never has it been the teacher, but the curriculum, never the doctor, but the model and the medicine, not the officers, but the law, and not the employee, but the policy, and nor is it the scientist, but instead it is the premise and this is the approach. And it is within all these processes and all these procedures that ooze down from on high, that now envelop and direct us within a mire of prejudicial ideals, methods of intolerance, racism, and ambigu ambiguous and diluted intention, that we are given continuing example and evidence of the establishment's advocacy and appetite for constraint, malpractice, and injustice. These conspicuous parallels of inactivity, heavy handedness, and bias that exist from one heartless institution to the next and from one defective system to the next, I believe it can be said to present a definite affinity towards density, thickness, and stagnancy, and as only partial but vital representations of the consistency and constitution of this systemic disability points again not to mutable objects, but instead to something fundamentally stubborn, sober, and cold. The pervasively influential, oppressive, and demoralizing conditions of the current human experience demands not only a profound recognition of our implicit subservience and to and dependence on established order, but as well the more perilous wholesale devaluation and abduction of our own sense of self. For as numbers, commoners of a general public, the aspects of personal relevance, importance, value, and worthiness are inspirations that remain without nurture within this disheartening enclosure. As individuals, our stature within and adjacent to this massive machine is regarded with little or no value. We are but numbers and faces, each with the same story, and without the haze of a climate dampened by dampened by cold disposition, demoralizing pretension, and shared consternation. There are heavy clouds cast over our psyches as we are forced into the knowing of our natural negligibility and take on submissive behaviors and timid self preserving silence. This customary demotion and disparagement of our personal significance extends beyond our psychological subordination to the establishment, as aside from being overly bullied and into cowering dependence on institutional supremacy for everything. With the same message, we are also we also find ourselves mentally enfeebled, confused, and resigned. And through the insolent assertions of discriminatory and degrading mental programming that comes forth from all manipulative influence of modern convention, there is no immunity to the imposed segregating principles and the discourse that ultimately manifests itself within us as a deprivation of free thinking, compulsive discriminatory impairment, and inbred racism, and an appropriated competence for contemplative discernment. We draped in threadbare, soiled, and shrunken clothing are given little cover from the fallout of ongoing suggestive narratives that deplete us and charge us with inferiority and unworthiness. We devotedly concede to our diminutive roles and are subdued in dispassionate suppression and passively accept our meekness, our incapacity, and ineligibility to augment our own cognitions, self reliance, and interpretations of reality. The power, though, that we think we hold and the voice that we think we have is only what we are allotted and one that may be used only to express the preferable means by which we will continue to be controlled. Yes, we have the right to free choice as long as we choose from their list. Yes, we have the right to free to freely gather and to protest where it is we are told. We can freely take a stand against tyranny, but with respect, and we are free to use our voices as long as we are not too loud. We can stand, we can rebel in orderly fashion, and we can revolt, but only placidly, as constantly there looms in our periphery the knowing of the might and the severity and the swiftness with which we can and will be dealt. And indeed, it is ludicrous to believe that we who are subordinate in every seen and unnoticed capacity to the institution would in any way actually have a say in the shaping and engineering of our own servitude, and that our desires, our needs, and our dreams within this construct are somehow significantly persuasive through some united plebeian consensus to stipulate and determine intent or outcome. With pencil and privacy cube, we are defrauded into a false sense of empowerment and importance as we are persuaded with misleading propaganda to responsibly make our meaningless declarations and designations and to forcibly accept and validate one or more of the many predetermined and predestined choices of ambiguous confounding and double dealing candidates or legislations. We are only being led to believe that our voices are being heard and that real change is underway. And on occasion, we are given a trophy for our diligent efforts to ease our plight, whether it be by favorable candidate measure or enactment, tax relief, or pathetically small stimulus check. We are placated with the most minimal of victories as the true public outcry for change, relief, and fucking mercy falls on the deafened ears of our indifferent keepers. And it should be without doubt to anyone that our freedoms and the weight of our chains is really not ours to decide.

Despite all the suffering, despite all the struggle, and no matter how loud we scream, it is our submission to servility that this conglomerate invested invest its holdings, and it is only within its accredited sanctuary of subservience that we will ever see any share of its returns. Through the mandated compliance of permissible and gratuitous requirements that are and with predesignated appropriate attitudes and behaviors, every aspect of our lives is in one way or another dimmed or adulterated by the ongoing demands of institutional control. However, as moderated absolutism isn't possible and clemency is so far from its soul, in the wake of this oppressive mental and fiscal looting and under the cracking whip of untold numbers of demands, we remain browbeaten, tamed, tormented, and with little understanding or hope that things could ever be any different. But through our willingness to explore and to exploit the truth of our captive realities, and as we begin to take notice of the grotesque misguidance, the misrepresentation, and misuse that is the very furniture and tapestry of the cold and shadowy halls of our indoctrination and handling, We also allow ourselves to deepen our insight and to gain greater understanding of what it is that truly lies at the core of this modern aggregate and why everywhere there seems such suffering and such strife. I believe it is only with the awareness of what constitutes our bindings can we know with what to dissolve them. And as we awaken to the real illness and calamity of this institution, we will find concealed within its multitude of dysfunctional conditions a rampant infestation of unprincipled yet calculated recklessness that signifies the severity of insolent imprudence, dishonesty, and foolishness that ultimately drives this institution's actions. And in the vast disproportion of these decisively negative and unfavorable attributes versus what is the far lesser degree of virtuous and beneficial ones, we are given clear and ample evidence towards a proper diagnosis and treatment for this staggering and diseased formation. For something so out of balance and completely overrun by such a broad number of unscrupulous inclinations, one cannot help but recognize the extraordinary deficit of those things therein that are decent and righteous. And in the pursuit of relief from the weight of our hardships, and by taking note of the many layers of heavy constrictions that burden us, it becomes increasingly relevant to properly interpret the essence of these encumbrances, to recognize that within all things there is embodied an essential nature, and whether that nature aligns with positivity, health, or goodness, or with negativity, disease, and pain, that it can be witnessed, identified, and understood by looking to the expressions of a thing's predominant governing qualities and traits. Where, for example, there is much pressure, restriction, tension, oppression, imposition, and cramping, where there is always heaviness, where there is always burden, where there is compaction and there is constraint, where there is density and thickness, where things are frozen and they do not flow, where there is no movement, no change, no progress, where there is dormancy and congestion, strangulation and a gasping for error. Where there is no expansion, there is no room for gain, no room for growth. There is also no room for wellness. There is no room for life. There is no room for love, and there is no room for light.
